subject: Private deployment pricing: environment counts, license model & token econ follow-up
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Ari Patel <ari.patel@opslyte.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + numbers we discussed (private/VPC pricing)

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear breakdown of Opslyte's staging/prod needs. Below is a short recap so we can make sure our pricing proposal aligns with your budget and usage expectations. Please correct anything I got wrong.

Recap of your inputs from the call:
- Workloads: customer-facing inference (chat + summarization) + nightly batch embedding jobs.
- Expected Q3 steady-state token volume: 250M tokens/month (peak bursts up to ~1B).
- Environment count: 2 prod clusters (us-west + us-east), 1 shared staging, and a sandbox for dev (total 4 environments).
- Security/ops: SOC 2 required, KMS integration, VPC peering, retention 90 days.
- Timeline: pilot in 6–8 weeks, production early Q4.

Open asks from our side to give a concrete proposal:
1) Confirmation of budget range for private deployment (annual committed spend). Even a broad band helps: <$150k, $150–350k, $350k+.
2) Desired support level: Standard (business hours), Premium (24x7), or Enterprise (dedicated TAM + SLA).
3) Whether you prefer a reserved-capacity licensing model (monthly/annual commit + per-token overage) or an on-prem/perpetual license with annual maintenance.
4) Any constraints on on-host telemetry or audit log retention beyond 90 days.

For context on unit economics we discussed on the call: our target ballpark for similar customers running private/VPC setups with these environment counts has been $800–$1,400 per 1M tokens in fully reserved scenarios (includes reserved GPU capacity, orchestration, retention, and basic support). If you prefer an on-prem perpetual model, the upfront license + 18–20% yearly maintenance tends to shift costs front-loaded but lowers per-token marginals (we can model both).

Next steps
- If you can confirm the budget band and preferred support tier, I’ll route this to Karthik and Ben for a formal quote + an appendix with 2 pricing scenarios (reserved monthly commit vs. on-prem license) and a worked example for 250M tokens/month.
- Also attaching a quick ops worksheet (opslyte_pilot_scope.xlsx) we filled during the call — please add anything missing.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: opslyte_pilot_scope.xlsx (spreadsheet stub: env counts, peak/steady token rows)

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + numbers we discussed (private/VPC pricing)

Stephanie — thanks for the clear recap. Quick clarifications:
- Budget band: leaning toward $150–350k for the first year (pilot + ramp). If the economics look favorable we can expand commit in year 2.
- Support: need Premium for the first 6 months (we want 24x7 on-call during pilot ramp), then likely downgrade to Standard for steady-state.
- License preference: open to either; ops wants to see a committed-reserved example first.
- Telemetry: need audit logs for 180 days for compliance, ok to keep obfuscated PII in logs.

Also, the token profile is slightly skewed: chat is the bulk (~70% of tokens), batch embeddings are heavy on the backend nightly window. For the pilot we expect 80M–120M tokens/month and will scale.

I attached a marked-up pilot scope (see attachment) with the environment breakdown.

Ari

Opslyte

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Jul 2026 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Quick follow-up + numbers we discussed — opslyte confirmation and asks

Steph / Ben — draft numbers below. These are high-level estimates (engineering will refine capacity once we validate the model size & seq lengths). I prioritized clarity so we can get this over to Opslyte and iterate.

Scenario A — Reserved monthly commit (recommended for pilot-to-prod ramp):
- Pilot footprint (100M tokens/mo steady): reserve 2 GPU nodes per prod region equivalent (N1 x A100-class equiv) + 1 small staging node + shared sandbox (total reserved nodes: 5)
- Monthly reserved cost: $28,500/month (reserved GPU amortized + orchestration + SOC2 infra add-ons)
- Included support: Premium for first 3 months (cost included), then Standard.
- Token equivalence: at pilot profile we estimate ~1.1M tokens per reserved-dollar efficiency -> implied cost ~ $820 / 1M tokens for pilot (includes infra & ops).

- Production footprint (250M tokens/mo steady): reserve additional nodes (total nodes: 10), monthly reserved cost ~ $72,000/month.
- Implied cost at 250M tokens ~ $860 / 1M tokens (economies of scale offset replication & cross-region traffic).
- Overage rate: $1.25 / 1k tokens (applies if sustained monthly > commit).

Scenario B — On-prem perpetual license + maintenance (alternative):
- Upfront license: $420,000 (includes runtime & orchestration license for specified envs, SOC2 kit), delivery & install one-time $45,000.
- Annual maintenance (18%): $75,600/year covering updates, security patches, 5x8 support. Premium on-call is add-on.
- Infra estimate: customer-borne GPU fleet equivalent to 10 nodes for 250M tokens. If Opslyte already owns infra, this lowers TCO.
- Implied token cost (amortized over 3 years incl infra ops estimate): ~$640–$750 / 1M tokens (depending on capex assumptions). Break-even vs reserved model happens ~18–30 months depending on utilization and infra economics.

Notes / line items to include in customer doc:
- Audit log storage delta for 180-day retention: add ~$1,200/month for cross-region replication and encrypted storage for logs at their scale.
- KMS integration & key-management: one-time professional services $12k.
- SLA & support: premium 24x7 for pilot included in reserved pricing; add $6k/month if they want 24x7 post-pilot.

Next steps:
- I’ll convert these into a two-page pricing appendix and a one-page run-rate comparison (shows $/1M token lines for 100M & 250M). Steph, if this looks right I’ll attach the appendix and the redwood-vpc-pricing-options.pdf and send to Ari.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
